articles.title: Three Tankers, 94 Indian Sailors, and a Strait That Tried to Trap Them. They Finally Got Out.
articles.excerpt: As the first oil cargoes move again through the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S.–Iran ceasefire, the slow release of 94 Indian crew on three tankers is a reminder of who actually keeps the world's energy moving — and who pays the price when the chokepoint closes.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea; three Indian-flagged tankers carrying 94 crew cleared the Strait of Hormuz this week
articles.nri_angle: India supplies more than 300,000 of the world's seafarers — a largely working-class diaspora whose remittances sustain families back home and whose labour moves a fifth of the world's oil through the Strait of Hormuz; the release of 94 Indian crew on three tankers, after others were stranded and three were killed, shows how directly the Gulf crisis lands on Indian families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Box of Alphonsos Now Costs as Much as Lobster. The War in the Gulf Is Part of the Reason.
articles.excerpt: Indian mango season in America has become a full-blown diaspora frenzy — WhatsApp alerts, warehouse runs, $2,000 'mango passes.' But this year the Strait of Hormuz crisis has pushed airfreight costs up, even as a new hybrid variety, Sonpari, makes its U.S. debut at $70 a box.
articles.image_caption: Alphonso mangoes from India; diaspora demand has pushed premium boxes to lobster-tier prices in the U.S.
articles.nri_angle: Indian mango season has become a beloved summer ritual for the U.S. diaspora — a $40 box as 'a plane ticket home' — but the Strait of Hormuz war has pushed up the airfreight these delicate, must-fly fruit depend on, even as a new hybrid, Sonpari, debuts at $70 a box, tying the price of nostalgia directly to Gulf geopolitics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Citizenship Was Supposed to Be the Finish Line. The Justice Department Is Quietly Reopening Old Files.
articles.excerpt: A ramped-up federal denaturalization effort — a dedicated DOJ unit, a June memo listing ten priority categories, and a fresh batch of cases including the first in Oregon this term — is unsettling naturalized Indian-Americans who assumed the oath was the end of the immigration road, not a document the government could revisit.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. naturalization ceremony; a ramped-up DOJ effort is reopening the question of whether citizenship is final
articles.nri_angle: A sharply expanded federal denaturalization effort — a dedicated DOJ unit expecting 'several hundred' cases, a June memo listing ten priority categories, and the first Oregon case of the term targeting an Indian-origin man — is unsettling the roughly two million naturalized Indian-Americans who treated the citizenship oath as the irreversible end of their immigration journey.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Emergency-Room Doctor From Minneapolis Is About to Become the Diaspora's Newest Astronaut. Liftoff Is July 14.
articles.excerpt: Anil Menon — son of a Malayali father and a Ukrainian mother, SpaceX's first flight surgeon, and now a U.S. Space Force colonel — will launch aboard Soyuz MS-29 for an eight-month stay on the International Space Station, adding another Indian-origin name to the short, storied list of those who have left the planet.
articles.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who launches to the International Space Station aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14
articles.nri_angle: Anil Menon — the Minneapolis-born son of a Malayali father and Ukrainian mother, SpaceX's first flight surgeon and now a U.S. Space Force colonel — launches July 14 aboard Soyuz MS-29 for an eight-month ISS mission, adding another Indian-origin name to the lineage of Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams and Shubhanshu Shukla and giving the diaspora a rare moment of pride beyond the daily churn of immigration and trade news.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: For the First Time in Six Years, Indians Are the Most Deported Nationality From Canada
articles.excerpt: Canada removed 1,712 Indian citizens in the first quarter of 2026 — nearly a third of all deportations — and a record 6,980 Indian cases now sit in the removal queue, a sharp signal of how far the welcome mat has been pulled back for the country's largest immigrant community.
articles.image_caption: Toronto's skyline; Indians are now the largest nationality deported from Canada in 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indians are Canada's largest immigrant, student and temporary-worker community, so the country becoming its top deported nationality in 2026 — with a record 6,980 cases still pending removal — directly raises the stakes for hundreds of thousands of Indian families to track permit deadlines and file renewals early before a lapsed status hardens into a multi-year re-entry ban.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Gulf's Oil Is Flowing Again Through Hormuz. India Is in No Rush to Go Back.
articles.excerpt: With two months of crude already in tank and Russian barrels still cheap, Indian refiners are letting Middle Eastern suppliers wait — even as the war's legacy lingers in a record import bill and four straight hikes at the pump that diaspora families feel on every trip home.
articles.image_caption: A crude oil tanker; India is letting Gulf suppliers wait even as the Strait of Hormuz reopens
articles.nri_angle: India's strategy after the Hormuz reopening — staying on cheap Russian crude rather than rushing back to Gulf suppliers — directly shapes the rupee, the trade deficit and pump prices, the everyday inflation NRIs feel on remittances and every trip home after India absorbed a record energy bill and four fuel-price hikes during the war.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The UAE Just Gave Stranded Residents One Last Window. For Indians Caught by the Spring Airspace Chaos, the Clock Runs to July 9.
articles.excerpt: Abu Dhabi's identity authority has opened a final 30-day grace period — running June 10 to July 9 — for those who benefited from this spring's overstay-fine waivers, letting them regularise their status or leave penalty-free as the Gulf's largest Indian community sorts out paperwork left in limbo by the regional flight shutdowns.
articles.image_caption: Abu Dhabi's skyline; the UAE has opened a final 30-day visa grace period running to July 9, 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the UAE's largest expatriate community — over 3.5 million people — and many were left with lapsed or cancelled visas when regional airspace closed this spring; the ICP's final 30-day grace period to July 9, 2026 gives them a penalty-free path to either fix their status or leave, with a five-day consular service blackout (June 26–30) complicating the timeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Fed Just Hinted Its Next Move Is Up, Not Down. For NRIs, That Quietly Rewrites the Math on the Rupee and Their Dollar Savings.
articles.excerpt: In Kevin Warsh's debut meeting the Federal Reserve held rates but flipped its dot plot toward a 2026 hike — firming the dollar, pressuring the rupee, and reshaping the calculus for diaspora investors weighing US yields against India's newly sweetened NRI deposit rates.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, whose first meeting signalled rates could rise in 2026
articles.nri_angle: The Fed's hawkish turn under new Chair Kevin Warsh — a dot plot now pointing to a 2026 hike — strengthens the dollar and pressures the rupee, reshaping the trade-off NRIs face between elevated US yields and India's newly uncapped NRI deposit rates near 7 percent, and affecting the rupee value of every remittance sent home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Two Biggest Green-Card Doors Just Slammed Shut Until October. The July Visa Bulletin Spells It Out.
articles.excerpt: The State Department's July 2026 Visa Bulletin marks EB-2 and EB-5 (unreserved) for India as 'Unavailable' and retrogresses EB-1 India by two months — a fiscal-year freeze that strands tens of thousands of skilled Indian professionals just weeks before the annual reset.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. green card; the July 2026 Visa Bulletin marks EB-2 and EB-5 for India as 'Unavailable'
articles.nri_angle: The July 2026 Visa Bulletin marks EB-2 and EB-5 (unreserved) for India as 'Unavailable' and retrogresses EB-1 India — freezing the green-card lanes that tens of thousands of Indian engineers, doctors and researchers rely on until the fiscal-year reset on October 1, 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Germany Just Made Layovers Easier for Indian Travellers. Lufthansa Thinks That Changes the Map to America.
articles.excerpt: As of June 3, Indian passport holders no longer need a Schengen airport transit visa to change planes at Frankfurt or Munich — a quiet bureaucratic win that the Lufthansa Group now expects to redraw how the diaspora flies between India, the UK and the Americas.
articles.image_caption: Frankfurt Airport, a key transit hub for Indian travellers, where transit visas are no longer required
articles.nri_angle: Germany scrapped the Schengen airport transit visa for Indian passport holders effective June 3, 2026 — sparing students, professionals and families changing planes at Frankfurt or Munich the cost and paperwork of a Type A visa, and prompting Lufthansa to expect higher India traffic on routes to the UK and the Americas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Scrapped the Gulf's NEET Centres. Now Diaspora Families Are Flying Their Kids Home for Sunday's Re-Test.
articles.excerpt: After a paper leak forced India to cancel 2.3 million NEET results, the medical entrance exam is being re-run on June 21 — with every overseas centre closed and Telegram blocked nationwide to stop cheating rackets.
articles.image_caption: Families and guardians wait outside an entrance-examination centre in India as candidates sit the test.

sources.label: Reuters — 'India temporarily blocks Telegram app over medical exam fraud' (re-test June 21, 2.3 million results cancelled, Durov response)
Reuters — 'India med school hopefuls beset with anxiety before they retake scandal-tainted exam' (CBI probe, arrests, tightened security)
LiveLaw — 'Supreme Court Refuses To Hear Pleas Concerning NEET-UG 2026 Ahead Of June 21 Retest' (1,600 candidates, admit-card centre changes, Justice P.S. Narasimha bench)
Khaleej Times / EdArabia — 'UAE Students Under Pressure After India Closes International Centres for Medical Exam' (overseas centres scrapped, Gulf-parent accounts)

articles.nri_angle: India closed all 14 overseas NEET-UG centres for the June 21 re-test, forcing thousands of Gulf-resident Indian families to book flights, take leave and arrange accommodation in India so their children can sit a single three-hour medical-entrance exam.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The India-UK Trade Deal Finally Has a Date — and a Quiet Win for NRI Pay Packets
articles.excerpt: CETA and the Double Contribution Convention both take effect July 15. The tariff cuts grabbed the headlines, but the clause that exempts 75,000 Indian professionals from UK National Insurance for five years is the one diaspora workers will feel.
articles.image_caption: PM Narendra Modi receives UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in Mumbai, October 2025.

sources.label: GOV.UK — 'The countdown begins: UK-India FTA enters into force on July 15th' (June 17, 2026)
Reuters — 'UK-India trade deal worth over $6 billion to start July 15' (June 17, 2026)
India Ministry of Commerce & Industry via Livemint / Capital Market — 'India-UK CETA and Double Contribution Convention to come into effect from 15 July' (5-year exemption, 99% duty-free lines)
Madhyamam Online / Bloomberg — 'India-UK free trade agreement to take effect from July 15' (Modi-Starmer 'We did it' exchange; CBAM/steel delay backstory)

articles.nri_angle: The trade deal's social-security pact exempts more than 75,000 Indian professionals on temporary UK postings from paying UK National Insurance for up to five years — a direct, recurring pay rise for the diaspora workers who shuttle between India and Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dhaka's Hindus March by Torchlight, Chanting 'Jai Shri Ram,' After a Shoe Is Placed on Lord Ram
articles.excerpt: A halted 81-foot Ram statue and a desecrated idol have pushed Bangladesh's anxious Hindu minority into the streets — and pulled India, Washington and the diaspora into the fight over their safety.
articles.image_caption: A Durga Puja procession by members of Bangladesh's Hindu minority community in Dhaka.

sources.label: ANI / Daily Prabhat — 'Hindus in Bangladesh hold torchlight protest against alleged disrespect to Lord Ram' (June 19, 2026)
Devdiscourse / The CSR Journal — 'Bangladeshi Hindu students to stage massive protest against alleged insult to Lord Ram' (72-hour ultimatum, Gaibandha statue, June 2026)
Associated Press — 'Bangladesh's Hindu minority in fear as attacks rise and a national election nears' (violence data, Yunus government, Feb 2026)
ANI / India Tribune — 'India concerned over surge in extremist rhetoric in Bangladesh, calls on Yunus govt to protect minorities' (MEA statement)
The Indian Eye — 'US officials raise concern about democracy in Bangladesh' (congressional and State Department concern, June 2026)

articles.nri_angle: Much of the international pressure on Dhaka over attacks on Hindus comes from the diaspora itself, and many NRIs have family roots and relatives across the India-Bangladesh border whose safety is directly at stake.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Pilots Reject the AI171 'Suicide' Verdict. Their Simulator Says the Plane Failed, Not the Crew.
articles.excerpt: The Federation of Indian Pilots says new tests show the official four-second timeline is 'physically impossible' — and points to a catastrophic electrical failure on the London-bound Boeing 787 that killed 241.
articles.image_caption: Air India Boeing 787-8 VT-ANB, the aircraft that operated Flight AI171, at London Heathrow.

sources.label: Madhyamam / IANS — 'Electric failure led to Air India Boeing crash in Ahmedabad: Pilots’ body' (June 19, 2026)
ANI — 'Fuel switches moved without input, points to possible glitch: Federation of Indian Pilots Chief on AI171 crash report' (July 13, 2025)
The Sun — 'My wife died in the Air India crash… these questions need to be answered' (whistleblower electrical-failure evidence, June 2026)
Wikipedia — 'Air India Flight 171' (AAIB investigation timeline, EAFR recovery)

articles.nri_angle: AI171 was a London-bound flight full of British-Indian and NRI passengers, and the diaspora flies the same Boeing 787 fleet weekly — so whether the crash is blamed on dead Indian pilots or a systemic Dreamliner flaw is a question with direct personal stakes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's Tech Jobs Are Quietly Moving to Bengaluru. India's 'Capability Center' Workforce Is Nearing 2.4 Million.
articles.excerpt: As Washington tightens the H-1B route, US firms like N-able are opening Global Capability Centers in India and hiring frontier AI and cybersecurity talent on Indian soil — the mirror image of the visa fight.
articles.image_caption: International Tech Park in Whitefield, Bengaluru, a hub of India's Global Capability Center industry

sources.label: Reuters
Nasscom
Zinnov
The Economic Times

articles.nri_angle: The GCC boom rewrites the migration calculus for the diaspora: the cutting-edge job for an American company is increasingly available in Bengaluru or Hyderabad, without the visa lottery or green-card backlog — meaning a homecoming no longer has to be a career sacrifice.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Women Open Their World Cup With a 95-Run Demolition — and the Diaspora Has a Home Tournament in England
articles.excerpt: Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma powered India to 209 against the Netherlands at Headingley before the bowlers sealed a crushing win, as the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup unfolds across British-Indian heartlands.
articles.image_caption: India opener Smriti Mandhana, whose batting anchors the side at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup

sources.label: Cricbuzz
CricToday
Sportradar
The Indian Eye

articles.nri_angle: A Women's T20 World Cup staged across England puts India's rising women's side within reach of one of the world's largest Indian diasporas — a rare home tournament for British-Indian fans and a source of role models for diaspora daughters taking up the game from Southall to Sunnyvale.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Heading for Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years. The Bill Will Land on Dinner Tables — Including the Diaspora's.
articles.excerpt: A strengthening El Niño has left the 2026 monsoon delayed and deficient, with the IMD forecasting the lowest rainfall since 2015, Mumbai rationing water, and coffee, sugar and pulse crops already at risk.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)

sources.label: Reuters
The Hindu BusinessLine
India Meteorological Department
Dainik Bhaskar

articles.nri_angle: A failing monsoon stokes food inflation and pushes New Delhi toward rice and sugar export curbs — the moves that spike basmati and onion prices in diaspora grocery stores abroad — while pressuring the rupee and the returns NRIs earn on Indian deposits, and threatening the incomes of relatives still farming back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The $100,000 H-1B Fee Is Back. Indian Tech Workers Who Celebrated Its Defeat Have 72 Hours of Whiplash to Show for It.
articles.excerpt: A Boston judge struck down the fee on June 8, then paused his own order on June 12 — so as of June 17 the $100,000 charge is again in force, with conflicting rulings in three courts pointing toward the Supreme Court.
articles.image_caption: The Boston skyline; a federal judge in Boston struck down the H-1B fee on June 8, then paused his own order four days later

sources.label: Reuters
Associated Press
LiveLaw
The Indian Eye

articles.nri_angle: Nearly three-quarters of H-1B visas go to Indians, so a reinstated $100,000 fee threatens the principal on-ramp for Indian engineers, doctors and researchers — and the on-again, off-again legal whiplash forces diaspora families, students and physicians to make irreversible decisions against a rule that can flip in 72 hours.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is Entering the Home Stretch. America's Top Trade Negotiator Lands in Delhi Monday.
articles.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer visits India on June 23-24 to finalise the framework agreement, with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal predicting the first tranche could be executed by mid-July.
articles.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who says the first tranche of the India-US trade deal could be done by mid-July

sources.label: Reuters
The Hindu BusinessLine
The Indian Eye
Outlook Business

articles.nri_angle: A trade deal reshapes the fortunes of the Indian exporters, IT-services firms and pharma companies that employ diaspora professionals, and directly shifts costs for Indian-American importers of textiles, jewellery and generic drugs — while knitting the two countries the diaspora bridges ever closer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian IT Stocks Just Crashed to a Three-Year Low. One Warning From Accenture Did It.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index sank as much as 5.6 percent on June 19, with TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech falling 5-8 percent, after Accenture flagged cautious client spending and an AI-driven shift that threatens the sector's labour-heavy model.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru; the Nifty IT index sank to a three-year low on June 19

sources.label: Reuters
The Hindu BusinessLine
Mint
Barron's

articles.nri_angle: India's IT majors are the largest sponsors of H-1B visas and the biggest employers of diaspora technologists abroad, so a demand slowdown colliding with a tighter US visa regime and AI layoffs threatens the very job pipeline that carried many NRIs overseas — even as the sector's heavy weighting in the Nifty hits diaspora portfolios directly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Reliance Just Filed for the Jio IPO. It Could Be the Biggest Stock Debut in India's History.
articles.excerpt: At the Reliance AGM on June 19, Mukesh Ambani said Jio Platforms' draft prospectus was filed with SEBI — a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares targeting roughly $4 billion, on a business brokerages value near $180 billion.
articles.image_caption: Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani, who announced the Jio Platforms IPO filing at the AGM

sources.label: Reuters
The Hindu BusinessLine
The Wall Street Journal
Outlook Business

articles.nri_angle: The Jio IPO offers NRIs a rare large-cap, liquid way to own the infrastructure behind 500 million Indian internet users — investable through NRE/NRO portfolio accounts — and stands as a real-time referendum on whether the diaspora and the world still believe in India's digital growth story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Banks Want to Lend Dollars Out of GIFT City. The Target: $55 Billion in Diaspora Money.
articles.excerpt: Lenders are asking the RBI to route loans through their offshore GIFT City units to amplify a revived FCNR deposit scheme — a 2013-style bid to pull in diaspora dollars and steady a rupee just recovering toward 94.
articles.image_caption: The GIFT One tower at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, India offshore financial hub

sources.label: Reuters
Mint
Nomura research note

articles.nri_angle: New Delhi is openly competing for NRI savings: rising FCNR deposit rates, hedging subsidies and a proposed GIFT City lending mechanism could channel up to $55 billion in diaspora dollars into India, handing overseas Indians an outsized role in defending the rupee and earning more attractive, currency-risk-free returns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Quietly Rewrote Its Foreigner Registration Rules. NRI Families With Foreign-Passport Kids Need to Read the Fine Print.
articles.excerpt: The Immigration and Foreigners (Amendment) Rules, 2026 — in force since June 1 — scrap the old 14-day grace period for long-stay registration, allow late filing only in 'emergent circumstances,' and impose a new 30-day reporting duty on parents whose India-born child later takes a foreign citizenship.
articles.image_caption: A Republic of India Emergency Certificate, an official government travel document; new 2026 rules tighten registration duties for foreign nationals in India
articles.nri_angle: India's new 2026 immigration rules scrap the 14-day registration grace period for long-staying foreigners and impose a 30-day reporting duty on parents whose India-born child later acquires foreign citizenship — changes that directly affect OCI holders, NRIs with foreign-national spouses, and diaspora families raising children across two passports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Canada Want a Trade Deal Signed This Year. For Three Million Indians in Canada, the Reset Is Personal.
articles.excerpt: Meeting on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian — their fourth in under a year — Narendra Modi and Mark Carney pledged to conclude a long-stalled Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the G20, aiming to double bilateral trade to $50 billion and explicitly leaning on the diaspora as the bridge between the two countries.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney; the two leaders met on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian
articles.nri_angle: India and Canada set a G20 deadline to conclude a long-stalled trade deal and double bilateral trade to $50 billion — a reset that directly affects the roughly three million people of Indian origin in Canada through talent-mobility, student-exchange and services provisions, after a two-year freeze that hit the diaspora's people-to-people ties hardest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Told Banks to Pay NRIs Whatever It Takes. Deposit Rates Have Already Jumped to 7%.
articles.excerpt: In a move last used during the 2013 Taper Tantrum, the Reserve Bank has scrapped interest-rate ceilings on FCNR(B) and long-term NRE deposits until September 30 and is absorbing banks' hedging costs — a direct bid for the diaspora's dollars that has pushed rates from around 3% to as high as 7.1%.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai; the central bank scrapped rate caps on NRI deposits on June 17
articles.nri_angle: The RBI has temporarily lifted rate caps on FCNR(B) and long-term NRE deposits, pushing returns from ~3% to as high as 7.1% — a rare, time-limited chance for NRIs to earn high, low-risk returns on dollars or rupees parked in Indian banks, but only until September 30 and with tricky rules on breaking older deposits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Court Just Lifted a $100,000 Wall in Front of Immigrant Doctors. Indian-American Physicians Are Calling It a Win for Patients.
articles.excerpt: The American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin has welcomed a federal ruling striking down the Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B fee, warning the charge would have gutted rural and safety-net hospitals where international medical graduates — a large share of them Indian-trained — keep the lights on.
articles.image_caption: A United States federal courthouse; a federal judge struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee this week
articles.nri_angle: A federal court struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee that Indian-American physician group AAPI says would have crippled rural and safety-net hospitals — where Indian-trained doctors (21% of US immigrant physicians) are essential — but with an appeal likely and other anti-H-1B bills moving, the relief for the diaspora's medical community may be temporary.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Oil Lifeline Through Hormuz Is Reopening. The Peace Holding It Open Just Wobbled.
articles.excerpt: Tankers are moving through the Strait of Hormuz again after the US-Iran ceasefire, and an Indian-flagged ship is finally sailing home. But Friday's signing ceremony in Switzerland was scrapped, Iran is threatening transit fees, and roughly half of India's crude still rides on a 60-day truce.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea; tankers resumed transiting the Strait of Hormuz this week after the US-Iran ceasefire
articles.nri_angle: Roughly half of India's crude and a huge share of its trade ride through the Strait of Hormuz, where nearly half its overseas migrants and seafarers work — so the strait reopening means steadier Gulf jobs, cheaper goods and a calmer rupee, while the 60-day truce's fragility keeps diaspora-held energy and shipping stocks on edge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Handing Its UAE Passport and Visa Counters to a New Operator on July 1. Millions of NRIs Need to Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: From July 1, Al Hind Tours and Travels takes over passport, visa, OCI and attestation services across the Emirates — replacing BLS International and SGIVS Global. For the 3.5 million Indians in the UAE, every consular errand is about to run through a different door.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport; renewals, OCI cards and attestations in the UAE move to a new service provider on July 1
articles.nri_angle: Every passport renewal, OCI application and attestation for the 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the world's largest expatriate Indian community — moves to a new operator on July 1, so families should finish what they can before June 30 and trust only official Embassy channels for what comes next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Fuel Retailers Have Hit Their Borrowing Limit Absorbing Rs 1 Trillion in Losses to Keep Pump Prices Frozen
articles.excerpt: Oil secretary Neeraj Mittal says state-run IOC, BPCL and HPCL can barely borrow more after eating Rs 1 lakh crore of first-quarter losses to shield Indian consumers from the Iran war's oil shock. The freeze cannot hold forever — and the diaspora's families pay either way.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Oil fuel station; state retailers have absorbed about Rs 1 trillion in losses to keep pump prices frozen
articles.nri_angle: India has frozen pump prices through the oil shock by making state retailers borrow against Rs 1 trillion in losses — a cushion that keeps inflation and the relatives NRIs support protected for now, but whose eventual breaking point will hit household budgets, the rupee and diaspora-held energy stocks alike.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Hands Out Rs 2,400 Crore to First-Time Workers Today. It's a Bet That India's Jobs Problem Can Be Bought Down.
articles.excerpt: At Vigyan Bhawan on Friday, the Prime Minister disburses the first big tranche of the Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana — a Rs 99,446 crore scheme that pays young Indians to enter the formal economy and pays employers to hire them.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who disbursed Rs 2,400 crore under the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on June 19
articles.nri_angle: India is spending Rs 99,446 crore to pull its young workforce into the formal economy — a bet that, if it works, means households less dependent on diaspora remittances and a stronger demographic case for every NRI weighing an investment back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Years of Delay, India's Biggest Stock Exchange Files to Go Public. The NSE IPO Could Be Worth $57 Billion.
articles.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange — the world's busiest derivatives market — has finally filed draft IPO papers, setting up a $2.6 billion windfall for its investors and a landmark listing that lands just as India throws its equity markets open to NRIs.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, which filed draft papers for a landmark IPO
articles.nri_angle: India is listing the exchange at the heart of its markets just as it raises the limits on how much NRIs can own in Indian companies — a one-two move that courts the diaspora as a permanent class of domestic-market investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Rewrote the Rulebook for 4.5 Million OCI Holders. The Fine Print Forces a Hard Choice on Dual-Passport Families.
articles.excerpt: A sweeping overhaul moves Overseas Citizen of India casework fully online and promises 15-day approvals, but a mandatory passport-update rule with fines, colliding with new US disclosure demands, leaves diaspora families caught between two governments.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport and travel documents; India has overhauled the OCI program for its global diaspora
articles.nri_angle: OCI holders ARE the diaspora — 4.5 million of them — and this overhaul both speeds up their casework and, colliding with new US disclosure rules, forces dual-passport families into a long-deferred choice between an American and an Indian passport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai Has 40 Days of Drinking Water Left, and the Monsoon Is Running on Empty
articles.excerpt: The city is enduring its driest June in over a decade as reservoirs sink to roughly 10 per cent of capacity, forcing water cuts on construction and industry while Maharashtra waits on a monsoon that may be the weakest in 11 years.
articles.image_caption: The Mumbai skyline; the city is enduring its driest June in over a decade as reservoirs run low
articles.nri_angle: The huge Mumbai and Maharashtra diaspora has family weathering the cuts firsthand, while a weak monsoon stokes food inflation that quietly raises the real cost of the money NRIs send home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Arms Factories Just Hit a Record, and the Private Sector Is Finally Getting a Real Cut
articles.excerpt: Defence production touched an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY26 as exports surged past ₹38,000 crore — the clearest sign yet that India's bid to turn from the world's biggest arms importer into a maker and seller is gaining traction.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who announced India's record defence production for FY26
articles.nri_angle: A diaspora that has long watched India rank as the world's biggest arms importer now sees it building and exporting its own security, with the defence-tech boom drawing in exactly the high-skilled, globally networked talent the diaspora is full of.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.nri_angle: The exchange rate decides what every remitted dollar is worth to family in India, and NRIs weighing FCNR and NRE deposits now face a rare window of high deposit rates and a still-cheap but recovering rupee.
